data.title: US Equity Indexes Slump as Clouds Hovering Over Chipmakers, Hawkish Fed Outweigh Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut This Week
data.description:
04:22 PM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- US equity indexes slumped as Anthropic's (ANT) biggest-ever public listing and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blowout results failed to overcome the Federal Reserve's hawkish tone and tightening noose around chip exports.

* The S&P 500 closed at 6,921.31 on Friday, versus 7,554.86 a week ago. The Nasdaq Composite stood at about 22,660.75, compared with 25,132.43 a week earlier. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at 48,154.12, relative to 52,297.73 last week.

* The Commerce Department said it is seeking to ensure that existing restrictions on access to US advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers cannot be circumvented via remote computing arrangements involving third-country data centers.

* Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares were hit after Hunterbrook Media claimed that blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems continued using newer versions of the US chipmaker's firmware in its products.

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) is set to come under investigation by Democratic Party lawmakers over its influence on the US Commerce Department and its ability to circumvent restrictions on selling chips to China, Reuters reported, citing a letter by members of the House of Representatives.

* Anthropic's (ANT) shares dropped 8.5% on Friday, a day after the AI model developer closed its initial public offering of 1.13 billion shares of class A common stock at $83 each, raising about $93.5 billion in gross proceeds.

* The US 10-year Treasury yield sank 12.5 basis points to 4.92% Friday as investors sought the safety of government bonds. Gold futures plunged 4.5% as Fed speakers warned on inflation risks.

* The Federal Open Market Committee was in overwhelming agreement that further rate tightening will be needed given their inflation outlook, the October meeting minutes showed. The ongoing AI buildout is putting upward pressure on inflation, though productivity gains could help in easing such pressures, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said.

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX posts steepest weekly decline since 2020, confirms a correction
data.description:
(Updates at market close)

By Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index tumbled to a seven-month low on Friday and posted its sharpest weekly decline in six years, as investors worried that an uncertain global economic outlook could slow demand for commodities.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended down 838.88 points, or 2.5%, at 33,189.85. It was the seventh straight day of declines, which is the longest daily losing streak since October 2023, and the lowest closing level since April 6.

For the week, the index was down 8.1%, marking the steepest weekly decline since March 2020. The TSX has pulled back more than 10% from its record closing high on August 25, confirming the index has entered correction territory.

"As Middle East talks continue and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continues to rebound, the war premiums built into commodities appear to be fading, replaced by concerns over the future of resource demand in an uncertain economy," Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management, said in a note.

US crude oil futures settled 0.9% higher at $83.98 a barrel but still notched their third straight weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East. Gold floundered to a 14-month low, pressured by a hawkish interest rate outlook and an AI-linked selloff on Wall Street.

"Unfortunately, gold is not acting like the hedge it should in this environment. It's been acting more like a risk-on trade," said Sadiq Adatia, chief investment officer at BMO Global Asset Management.

The S&P 500, the US benchmark, posted an even steeper decline as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes the listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns.

The TSX's technology sector fell 6.1%, with shares of electronic equipment company Celestica ( CLS ) down 16.4%.

The materials sector, which includes metal mining shares, lost 5% and heavily weighted financials ended 2.5% lower.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith in Toronto and by Anand Gopal and Sudeshna Ghoshal in Bengaluru; Editing by Diti Pujara and Chris Reese)

data.title: Verlinvest to Facilitate China Resources’ Full Exit From Oatly
data.description:
• Proposed facilitation of China Resources’ exit from Oatly ( OTLY ) requires a tender offer because of Swedish law requirements
  • Verlinvest recommends that Oatly ( OTLY ) shareholders and holders of ADSs do not tender their shares or ADSs.

BRUSSELS--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Verlinvest, the global, family-backed consumer-focused evergreen investment company, today announced it has entered into an agreement to acquire China Resources Enterprise, Limited’s (“China Resources”) indirect interests in Oatly Group AB ( OTLY ) (“Oatly”), the world’s original and largest oat drink company. The transaction builds on Verlinvest’s investment in Oatly ( OTLY ) since 2016 and reinforces its conviction in the company’s long-term potential.

A change in strategic direction of state-owned enterprise China Resources informed its decision to fully exit its investment in Oatly ( OTLY ). China Resources worked constructively with Verlinvest to identify the best path for it to do so in recognition of the complexity of their joint holding structure.

Under the agreement, Verlinvest will acquire China Resources’ indirect interests in Oatly’s equity and convertible instruments that are currently held through Verlinvest and China Resources’ joint venture vehicle, Nativus Company Limited.

The transaction reflects the complexity of the Nativus ownership structure and under Swedish law, Verlinvest is required, as a condition to the transaction, to make a tender offer to all Oatly ( OTLY ) shareholders and holders of American Depositary Shares (ADSs). The tender offer commenced today. The tender offer price reflects the agreed terms and complex structure of Verlinvest’s transaction with China Resources and should not be interpreted as reflecting the fair value of Oatly’s shares or Verlinvest’s view of Oatly’s prospects. Verlinvest recommends that Oatly ( OTLY ) shareholders and holders of ADSs do not tender their shares or ADSs.

As a result of the transaction, Verlinvest’s ownership is expected to increase to approximately 42.6% of Oatly’s share capital. Verlinvest intends to continue working closely with Oatly’s management team and independent directors to support the company’s profitable growth strategy. China Resources’ three Board representatives are expected to step down from the Board following completion of the transaction. Verlinvest does not intend to take Oatly ( OTLY ) private or delist its ADSs from Nasdaq, upon completion of the transaction.

Roberto Italia, Chief Executive Officer of Verlinvest, said: “We first invested in Oatly ( OTLY ) ten years ago, when it was generating around $50 million in revenue, because we saw the brand at the forefront of a profound global shift towards taste-led, healthier and more sustainable food choices. Since then, Oatly ( OTLY ) has become an iconic, category-defining, global brand, generating over $860 million in revenue in 2025, and our conviction in its long-term potential is as strong as ever. Our decision to increase our investment reflects our confidence in Oatly’s management team, profitable growth strategy and the opportunities ahead.”

About Verlinvest

Verlinvest is an international, family-backed evergreen investment company. Verlinvest identifies inflection points in consumer behaviours and partners with the businesses driving these consumer revolutions forward while having a positive impact. Established in 1995, with offices in Brussels, London, New York, Singapore, and Mumbai, Verlinvest focuses on the FMCG, health, consumer technology and lifestyle categories, investing across three strategies: Venture, Growth, and Platform — from early-stage backing through large-scale brand building. The company has over €2.5bn in AUM and counts brands such as Oatly ( OTLY ), Vita Coco, Tony’s Chocolonely, Purplle, K1 Speed, Mutti, Who Gives A Crap, and Insomnia Cookies among its portfolio, alongside alumni Chewy, Sula, and Vitaminwater. data.title: Avenzo Therapeutics Announces Closing of Merger with Rallybio Corporation and Previously Announced $215 Million Concurrent Private Placement
data.description:
Merger creates Nasdaq-listed, clinical-stage oncology company; shares expected to begin trading as “AVZO” on November 23, 2026

Positive preliminary AVZO-1418 Phase 1 data recently presented at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on November 18, 2026

First of three clinical data readouts completed with AVZO-1418; two additional readouts planned prior to year-end 2026, with additional pipeline updates expected in 2027

Pro forma cash position expected to fund operations into late 2028

Conference call and webcast to discuss next steps for Avenzo as a public company, including review of recent data release for AVZO-1418, scheduled for November 23, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EST

SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Avenzo Therapeutics, Inc. (“Avenzo”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation oncology therapeutics, today announced the completion of its previously announced merger (the “Merger”) with Rallybio Corporation ( RLYB ) (“Rallybio”) , which closed on November 20, 2026. The combined company is operating under the name Avenzo Therapeutics, Inc., and its shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market on November 23, 2026, under the ticker symbol AVZO. The combined company will be led by Athena Countouriotis, M.D., its Chair, President and Chief Executive Officer, and other members of the Avenzo management team.

“We are pleased to complete this merger and launch Avenzo as a public company, with a pipeline of four potentially best-in-class or first-in-class clinical stage product candidates,” said Dr. Countouriotis. “We are excited by the positive preliminary AVZO-1418 data we presented this week at ENA, and we look forward to two additional clinical data presentations before year-end: initial Phase 1 data for AVZO-103, to be presented by our partner VelaVigo, and updated Phase 1 data for AVZO-023. With our strong balance sheet, I believe Avenzo is well positioned to deliver much-needed therapies to patients and create meaningful value for our stakeholders.”

Recent AVZO-1418 Data Update

On November 18, 2026, Avenzo announced positive preliminary Phase 1 data from the AVENTINE-1 study of AVZO-1418, its potentially best-in-class EGFR/HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium. The data showed responses in five of eight tumor types, including an objective response rate of 63% in 19 evaluable patients with heavily pretreated EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, the majority of whom were receiving 3rd line or later treatment. AVZO-1418 also demonstrated a favorable safety profile with a low incidence of Grade 3/4 hematologic adverse events. Based on these results, Avenzo is pursuing a rapid development plan that includes global expansion and further evaluation of AVZO-1418 in multiple tumor types. Additional details are available in Avenzo’s November 18, 2026 press release.

Upcoming Data Presentations

Avenzo expects two additional clinical data presentations before year-end 2026. On December 4, 2026, Avenzo’s partner in China, VelaVigo, will present initial Phase 1 data for VBC-103 in an oral presentation at ESMO Asia. On December 9, 2026, Avenzo will present updated Phase 1 data from the ORION-1 study of AVZO-023 in combination with fulvestrant at the San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium.

Reverse Merger Closing Conditions

Immediately prior to the closing of the Merger, Avenzo completed a previously announced oversubscribed private placement financing generating approximately $215 million in gross proceeds, with participation from a syndicate of leading healthcare institutional investors and mutual funds. This financing, together with existing cash, is expected to fund operations into late 2028, including multiple anticipated clinical milestones.

Immediately following the closing of the Merger and giving effect to the previously announced 1-for-2 reverse stock split of Rallybio ( RLYB ) common stock, the combined company had approximately 104.2 million shares of common stock issued and outstanding. On a fully diluted basis using the treasury stock method, pre-Merger Avenzo equity holders (excluding their participation in the private placement) owned approximately 56.6%, pre-Merger Rallybio equity holders owned approximately 2.8%, and investors in the private placement owned approximately 40.6% of the combined company’s common stock.

In connection with the Merger, Rallybio ( RLYB ) previously announced a special cash distribution of $83.6 million, or $13.90 per share, payable to stockholders and pre-funded warrant holders of record as of November 5, 2026, subject to Nasdaq due bill procedures. Shares of Rallybio ( RLYB ) common stock traded during the period from November 5, 2026, through the close of trading on November 20, 2026, carried due bills entitling buyers, rather than sellers, to the distribution, even if settlement occurs later. Accordingly, Rallybio ( RLYB ) common stockholders must have held their shares through the close of trading on November 20, 2026, to be entitled to the distribution. November 23, 2026 is expected to be the first day the combined company’s common stock will trade ex-dividend under the ticker symbol AVZO; purchasers on or after that date will not be entitled to receive the distribution on those shares. The scheduled distribution payment date is November 30, 2026.

In addition, eligible holders of Rallybio ( RLYB ) securities are expected to receive contingent value rights (CVRs) providing for potential payments from the monetization of Rallybio’s legacy assets, subject to the terms and conditions of the CVR agreement.

Conference Call and Webcast

Avenzo will host a listen-only conference call and audio webcast on Monday, November 23, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EST to discuss the closing of the Merger and the combined company’s pipeline and clinical development plans. There will be no question-and-answer session.

The webcast will be available on the company’s website, www.avenzotx.com, under the Events & Presentations section. Participants may also listen by phone by dialing +1 833-461-5787 (U.S. toll-free) or +1 585-542-9983 (international) and referencing conference ID 270 779 804.

An archived replay of the webcast will be available on the website for approximately 90 days following the call.

Advisors

Leerink Partners served as exclusive financial advisor to Avenzo. Evercore served as lead financial advisor and Citizens Capital Markets & Advisory served as co-financial advisor to Rallybio ( RLYB ). Cooley LLP served as legal counsel to Avenzo. Ropes & Gray LLP served as legal counsel to Rallybio ( RLYB ).

Leerink Partners, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Piper Sandler, and Guggenheim Securities served as placement agents for the private placement, and Mintz, Levin, Cohn, Ferris, Glovsky and Popeo, P.C. served as legal counsel to the placement agents.

About Avenzo Therapeutics

Avenzo Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing next-generation oncology therapeutics for patients. The company’s pipeline includes potentially best-in-class small molecules and bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Avenzo’s small molecule inhibitors, AVZO-021 and AVZO-023, are novel, highly potent and selective inhibitors of CDK2 and CDK4, respectively, which are key enzymes involved in cell cycle regulation. AVZO-021 is being evaluated in a Phase 1/2 study as monotherapy in advanced solid tumors and in combination with fulvestrant in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer. AVZO-021 and AVZO-023 are being evaluated in the Phase 1/2 ORION-1 study in patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, with AVZO-023 administered in combination with endocrine therapy, with or without AVZO-021. Avenzo’s first ADC drug candidate, AVZO-1418, is an EGFR/HER3 bispecific ADC that is being studied in the AVENTINE-1 Phase 1/2 study for the treatment of solid tumors. Avenzo’s second ADC drug candidate, AVZO-103, is a Nectin4/TROP2 bispecific ADC that is being studied in the BEACON-1 Phase 1/2 study for the treatment of advanced solid tumors. Avenzo is headquartered in San Diego, California. For more information, visit www.avenzotx.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: Wall St ends sharply lower on AIÂ selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries over the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes ended sharply lower. The Dow and the S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming both indexes have entered correction.

The bellwether S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

All three indexes logged their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq dipped into negative territory for the year.

"This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, appears to be accelerating to a certain degree," Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management in Billings, Montana. "But as we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day today."

"Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate space, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time," Northey added, referring to economic strength and solid corporate earnings, among other things.

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares posted a steep loss.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

"Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6% in mid-June. That luster has faded.

Hyperscalers Amazon and Meta tumbled.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius also posted steep losses on the day.

The tech selloff has prompted a rotation into more defensive sectors such as staples and healthcare.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 257.38 points, or 3.59%, to end at 6,918.45 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 1,225.05 points, or 5.13%, to 22,654.15. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 908.88 points, or 1.85%, to 48,188.18.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing a near-certain likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

A report from the University of Michigan survey showed post-election consumer sentiment rose to 7.3%.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth rose after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar shares lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

Bitcoin dropped below the $60,000 level, weighing on cryptocurrency firms including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.description:

By Julie Ingwersen

CHICAGO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Chicago soybean futures rose about 1% on Friday on export demand for soymeal and expectations of tightening US soybean inventories, analysts said.

Corn and wheat futures declined on a lack of supportive news but stayed above multi-month lows set a day earlier.

On the Chicago Board of Trade, January soybean futures settled up 13-1/4 cents, or 1.1%, at $12.20-3/4 per bushel. January soymeal ended up $9.40, or 2.8%, at $340.30 per short ton.

CBOT March corn finished down 3-3/4 cents, or 0.83%, at $4.48-3/4 a bushel and March wheat settled down 3 cents, or 0.5%, at $5.92 a bushel.

The CBOT soy complex got a boost as the US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 100,000 metric tons of US soymeal, a high-protein feed ingredient, to Spain. Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies, analysts said.

Meanwhile, demand for soy products supported margins for US soy processors, bolstering the crushing pace. The National Oilseed Processors Association this week reported a record-large soybean crush for October.

"Exports are strong and the crush is strong, so realistically, the (soybean) ending stocks probably go down" in the USDA's next monthly supply/demand report, said Don Roose, president of Iowa-based US Commodities.

Corn and wheat futures drifted lower as a surge in the dollar this week hung over the markets, making US grains less competitive globally.

The dollar index fell on Friday after rallying to 19-month highs this week on mounting expectations for US interest rate hikes. The stronger US currency has created broad pressure on dollar-denominated commodities.

Traders were also disappointed by limited announcements on agricultural trade following US President Donald Trump's discussions with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping during an Asia-Pacific summit this week.

Fading hopes for de-escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine kept attention on disruption to Black Sea grain trade, which has in turn led to a surge in European Union exports.

But favorable South American crop prospects capped wheat and corn prices.

Argentina's 2026/27 wheat harvest is progressing with yields above expectations, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said on Thursday, estimating the crop at 23.4 million tons, the country's second-highest production.

data.title: Anthropic's post-debut stumble delivers reality check for AI trade
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Anthropic's much-hyped arrival on Wall Street fizzled out on Friday as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.

As the first large machine-learning model maker to go public, Anthropic is widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, and its listing had been viewed as a potential boost for a sector struggling to regain its footing.

But the stock was last trading at $87.28, about 10% below Thursday's close and not far from its $83 IPO price, while declines in other technology heavyweights suggested the listing had done little to stem the broader selloff.

"Anthropic faded relatively quickly. I don't think investors believe there's something inherently wrong with the company, management or business. I think they're just skeptical of this market," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth.

The AI boom has come under pressure over the past month as concerns mount that spending on the technology, expected by some estimates to top $1 trillion this year, is not generating returns quickly enough.

Fears of political hurdles to data center construction and the leadership turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia have also added to those worries.

"Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds.

Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia fell about 6% and Meta Platforms dropped nearly 3%. Amazon and Microsoft lost less than 1% each.

Chip stocks also slid, with AMD and Marvell Technology down over 8% each and Intel losing roughly 3%.

The focus now shifts to a potential listing by another AI leader, OpenAI, which could provide another test of investor appetite for AI stocks. OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year.

Despite a strong IPO pipeline of high-profile AI and infrastructure companies, many have pushed their IPO plans to 2027.

PATIENCE MAY PAY

Anthropic's stock could find support in the coming weeks. London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares by year-end.

Near-term volatility, however, could persist as the initial euphoria around the listing fades and investors assess whether a valuation of about 40 times sales over the past 12 months can be sustained.

But Morgan Stanley, the underwriter tasked with stabilizing Anthropic's shares after its market debut, closed a position meant to do that, the company said, removing a potential pillar of support for shares.

Anthropic had a fully diluted valuation of about $1.6 trillion at the latest price, and a market capitalization of $1.2 trillion based on shares outstanding.

"We favor patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results," said Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at US Bank Asset Management, adding that the current valuation "assumes years of rapid growth."

The debut has also done little to ease broader concerns about the health of the AI trade. Wall Street's main indexes ended sharply lower on Thursday, while futures pointed to further declines on Friday.

PARALLELS WITH SPACEX

Anthropic's IPO has drawn parallels with Elon Musk's SpaceX, whose June listing was the second-biggest on record.

Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares, surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion haul to become the biggest listing on record.

While the companies have different business models, some investors have pointed to SpaceX's sharp swings in the weeks after its debut as a reason for caution over buying Anthropic immediately after its listing.

"There's going to be some volatility like we had with SpaceX. A lot of people are going to have FOMO. I don't think there's any need to get on it on the first trade," said Rob Hackel, CEO of financial advisory and brokerage firm RF Lafferty & Co.

SpaceX shares fell more than 6%.

Retail investors traded about $772 million of Anthropic shares on Thursday, the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking the data in 2012.

The stock's sharp swings have left investors weighing the prospects of a rebound against further losses. Options trading, set to begin next week, could add to the volatility.

"It's not a good environment for Anthropic at the moment," said Carsten Hesse, head of index events at Berenberg.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant in Bengaluru; Additional reporting by Manya Saini, Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Echo Wang; Editing by Anil D'Silva and Vidya Ranganathan)

data.title: Take-Two shatters sales record as 'GTA VI' launches to massive fanfare
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" helped Take-Two Interactive, the publisher of the blockbuster game that is now a global cultural phenomenon, rake in nearly $4 billion in first-day sales.

Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, is not a household name despite its portfolio of massive hits, including the "Red Dead Redemption" franchise and the "NBA 2K" basketball series.

The game also sold 32.5 million units in pre-release and garnered $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, Rockstar Games said on Friday. That is nearly five times the roughly $800 million GTA V made on its first day in 2013. It was widely regarded as the best-selling videogame in the first 24 hours.

Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that the company sold 24.5 million copies of GTA VI and $2.36 billion in pre-order revenue.

Take-Two had stayed tight-lipped about GTA VI demand since it opened for pre-orders in June, limiting commentary to saying demand has been "unprecedented" or "far exceeding expectations."

"The title is so widely anticipated, consumers appear very, very excited, and all the press so far has been universally positive, but we still aren't ready to declare victory," CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Take-Two's earnings call earlier this month.

"We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs," he had said.

GTA VI MARKETING BLITZ

Take-Two has shelled out an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs for GTA VI, making it one of the most expensive entertainment projects.

Sensor Tower estimates that the game's promotional trailer, GTA VI "Extended Look", on Netflix in August helped drive a sixfold jump in pre-orders.

In Miami, which Vice City is based on, the city's NBA team celebrated the release on Wednesday with a Vice City-themed match.

Over the weekend, the company is hosting "GTA VI: The Festival" - a music show with a star-studded line-up that includes Grammy-winning rapper Cardi B, hip hop record producer Metro Boomin and rapper Travis Scott.

WHAT NEXT FOR TAKE-TWO?

Investors have been waiting to hear from Take-Two about its plans for a PC launch of GTA VI and an online version rollout. The online, multiplayer component of a videogame is crucial in turning the title into a recurring revenue engine.

Some industry analysts are expecting the PC launch and online mode in 2027.

Brokerage TD Cowen named Take-Two one of its 'Best Ideas' for 2027, with its analyst Doug Creutz upbeat about the company's financial prospects when the game releases online.

"The potential ceiling for GTA VI's long-term recurrent consumer spending performance is very high... 'when' and 'how big' the next GTA Online will be is the most important question for the stock, more so than GTA VI unit sales."

(Reporting by Deborah Sophia in Bengaluru; Editing by Leroy Leo, Sherry Jacob-Phillips and Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: Trump says he still backs Lutnick, urges Nvidia's Huang to apologize
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Friday he still supported Howard Lutnick, calling him "a very good businessman" as a scandal at AI chipmaker Nvidia raises questions about Lutnick's handling of Chinese chip sales.

Trump, speaking to reporters at a press conference following his trip to Asia this week, also said he discussed Nvidia's ( NVDA ) co-founder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping but gave no other details about their conversation.

Reports that Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive and ties to a suspected Chinese spy triggered his resignation and sparked investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

US Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican, told the Wall Street Journal earlier on Friday that Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings that US artificial-intelligence chips were being smuggled to China before the Nvidia scandal became public but stopped short of saying he should resign.

Democrats, who take over Congress in January, meanwhile are probing whether Lutnick used his office to help investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, which is controlled by his sons, avoid losses stemming from scrutiny of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) ties to a Chinese firm.

"I have not lost confidence. He's a different kind of a guy, very good businessman," Trump told reporters. "I think he's doing a very good job."

Trump also said he'd like to see the former Nvidia chief "make a big apology and go back," adding: "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant - he's a brilliant man.' He is."

His comments contradict those by his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who told CNBC in an interview earlier on Friday that the former Nvidia CEO did not come up in talks.

The New York Times reported on Friday that the suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang, has extensive ties to China's defense industry.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing, an aide to the Senate Banking chairman said on Friday, though a representative for Huang declined to comment. Huang is also scheduled to speak to US House lawmakers behind closed doors in early December.

(Reporting by Bo Erickson in Washington; additional reporting by Katharine Jackson and Susan Heavey in Washington and Rodrigo Ramirez in Mexico City; Editing by Sanjeev Miglani)

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US stocks extended their rout on Friday, putting the S&P 500 and the Dow on course to confirm corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries over the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes were sharply lower, with the Dow and the S&P 500 now more than 10% below their record closing highs reached on October 6. Should those levels hold, it would confirm both indexes entered corrections on that date.

The bellwether S&P 500 is poised to notch its seventh consecutive drop, which would mark its longest losing streak since February 2020.

All three indexes are on track to log their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq entered negative territory for the year.

"The question that lingers is are we in a bear market or not?" said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "This feels more to me like a correction within a bull market, which tend to be very violent and fast."

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares were down 10.2%.

"Nvidia ( NVDA ) reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," Carlson added. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6%in mid-June. That luster has faded, with the index's year-to-date advance having shrunk to 21.4%.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ) was off 3.1%, while Meta dropped 4.7%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius slid over 10% each.

The tech selloff has prompted a rotation into more defensive sectors such as staples and healthcare, which were up 1.5% and 0.7%, respectively.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 278.99 points, or 0.57%, to 48,818.07, the S&P 500 lost 147.76 points, or 2.06%, to 7,028.07 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 810.98 points, or 3.40%, to 23,068.22.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing in a 95.5% chance of an interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

A report from the University of Michigan survey showed post-election consumer sentiment rose to 7.3%.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 10.8% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth ( UNH ) rose 4.7% after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar ( CAT ) 3.6% lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.27-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 32 new highs and 965 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,208 stocks rose and 3,563 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.95-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 18 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 13 new highs and 692 new lows.

data.title: Sector Update: Financial Stocks Decline Friday Afternoon
data.description:
01:57 PM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were lower in Friday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index shedding 0.9% and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) down 0.6%.

The Philadelphia Housing Index was climbing 1.3%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) added 0.3%.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was falling 6.8% to $58,678, and the yield for 10-year US Treasuries was dropping 11 basis points to 4.94%.

In economic news, US consumer sentiment improved in November, led by "substantial" increases in expected business conditions following the midterm elections, while the year-ahead inflation outlook reached its lowest level since February, final results of a University of Michigan survey showed Friday. The main sentiment index increased 7.3% sequentially to 51.5 this month, higher than the preliminary reading of 51, according to the survey. The consensus was for the reading to come in at 51.6, according to a Bloomberg-compiled poll.

State-level data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday showed the unemployment rate fell in three states and Washington, DC in October, rose in one and held steady elsewhere. The largest unemployment rate decline was in Washington, DC, where it fell by 0.2 percentage point, followed by 0.1 percentage point declines in Florida, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania. Colorado's 0.3 percentage point increase was the only gain in the month. Despite the decline, Washington, DC still had the highest rate at 5.4% while the lowest rate was seen in North Dakota, at 2.0%.

In corporate news, Citigroup ( C/PN ) (C) underestimated risk-weighted assets at its UK trading subsidiary by $35 billion due to errors in trade-related calculations, prompting the bank to inject additional capital into the unit over the summer, The Wall Street Journal reported. Citi shares were falling 3.3%.

KKR's (KKR) Helix Digital Infrastructure is in talks to buy a majority stake in EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure in a deal that could value EdgeCore at $8 billion to $10 billion, Bloomberg reported. KKR shares were down 2.4%.

Robinhood (HOOD) faces a shareholder proposal calling for a review of its proxy-voting platform, with activist group As You Sow arguing that customers should have more options for casting votes on corporate matters, Reuters reported. Robinhood shares were falling nearly 7%.
